"The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook." At the same time, the FOMC’s move to the effective lower bound and large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, together with expanded repos, discount window easing, and dollar swap lines, align with research on the credit channel and financial accelerator showing that when conventional policy is constrained, balance-sheet tools and liquidity backstops can reduce external finance premia and stabilize spending (Bernanke–Gertler; Gertler–Gilchrist; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Oliner and Rudebusch). The Committee’s emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent objective and close monitoring of expectations is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting frameworks (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford), helping to anchor expectations as market-based inflation compensation falls. These actions should mitigate downside amplification even in a liquidity-trap-like environment (Leeper; Eichenbaum–Fuerst), though they cannot fully offset the real public-health shock. Net assessment: still negative near term, but less severe given the strength and breadth of the policy backstop.
